title: HTTP-front substitution and qualification
summary: Wire browser hosting is qualified by contract, not by implementation prejudice. A conforming front must serve the same browser bytes with correct MIME/path semantics and supply the same bootstrap contract while leaving the WebSocket gateway and authoritative application path unchanged. The recovery harness captures and compares that contract for Node-front versus ooRexx HTTP/HTTPS A/B testing.
invariants: Change one variable: replace only the HTTP front during A/B qualification.
Keep the WebSocket gateway, Queue Fabric bridge, ObjectQueueManager, Wire definitions and application state unchanged.
Compare served HTML/CSS/JS hashes and normalized /wire-ui/bootstrap output.
Do not use python -m http.server or another fallback as evidence for ooRexx HTTP/HTTPS qualification.
A dynamic bootstrap descriptor does not make the HTTP front the application server.
DESIGN-empty/SOURCE-working faults must be diagnosed separately from HTTP-front substitution.

provenance.claim: Development/recovery evidence; does not supersede the accepted v0.11 executable baseline.
